final_answer:
Let
\[
I=\int_0^1 xT(x)\,dx.
\]
Since \(T\) preserves Lebesgue measure and \(T^3(x)=x\) a.e., the three functions
\[
x,\qquad T(x),\qquad T^2(x)
\]
all have the uniform distribution on \([0,1]\). Also, by measure preservation,
\[
\int_0^1 xT(x)\,dx
=\int_0^1 T(x)T^2(x)\,dx
=\int_0^1 T^2(x)x\,dx.
\]

Set
\[
S(x)=x+T(x)+T^2(x).
\]
Then
\[
\int_0^1 S(x)^2\,dx
=
3\int_0^1 x^2\,dx+6I
=
1+6I.
\]
But
\[
\int_0^1 S(x)\,dx
=
3\int_0^1 x\,dx
=
\frac32,
\]
so by Cauchy-Schwarz/Jensen,
\[
\int_0^1 S(x)^2\,dx\ge \left(\frac32\right)^2=\frac94.
\]
Hence
\[
1+6I\ge \frac94,
\]
so
\[
I\ge \frac{5}{24}.
\]

This bound is attainable. For example, write \(x\) in its nonterminating ternary expansion
\[
x=0.a_1a_2a_3\cdots{}_3,
\]
outside the usual null set of ambiguous expansions, and define \(T\) by adding \(1\) mod \(3\) to every ternary digit:
\[
T(x)=0.(a_1+1)(a_2+1)(a_3+1)\cdots{}_3 \pmod 3.
\]
Then \(T\) preserves Lebesgue measure, \(T^3=\mathrm{id}\) a.e., and for every ternary digit position the three orbit digits are \(0,1,2\), so
\[
x+T(x)+T^2(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}3\cdot 3^{-n}=\frac32
\]
a.e. Therefore equality is achieved.

Equality in Jensen occurs exactly when \(S(x)\) is constant a.e. Thus the necessary and sufficient condition for attaining the minimum is
\[
x+T(x)+T^2(x)=\frac32
\quad\text{for a.e. }x\in[0,1].
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{5}{24}}
\]
